title: Notes et dessins sur la generation et le mecanisme des fonctions intimes
shelf_note: No tradition set; collections are the source ones (getty, americana). A 1901 Rouveyre facsimile of Leonardo's Windsor anatomical leaves belongs in a library of early modern science. The `language: Italian` field describes Leonardo's leaves; the printed matter on these pages is French.
structure_note: The run is a blank verso, a pasted printed label ('Feuillet n° 13. . . Verso.'), and another blank: normal for a facsimile portfolio with interleaved guard sheets. The 3 printed backsteps / 1 repeat among only 8 numbered pages are almost certainly these leaf labels ('Feuillet n° N Recto/Verso') read as page numbers, not a disorder. Images 88 and 90 look alike (same stain pattern low on the sheet) but the files differ in size and blank versos of adjacent guard sheets would look like this; I cannot tell a duplicate scan from the images. The counter field pages_translated=46 disagrees with 98 page records carrying a translation (stale counter; many of the 98 are the system 'Blank page' string).

title: Le Nuove Musiche
shelf_note: Caccini's Le nuove musiche (Florence, Marescotti, dated 1601), BNCF copy; early modern music, in scope for the BNCF collection.
structure_note: Every image in the run is an unsplit two-page opening (18|19, 20|21, 22|23), so the 33 records are openings, not pages. Staff notation is described, not transcribed (25 of 33 records have OCR, 23 a translation).

title: Incomplete manuscripts
shelf_note: A bundle of unrelated Tibetan fragments from the Ogyen Choling collection (BL): Buddhist tantric ritual, at the edge of the library's scope, with no tradition or collection set. Title is a cataloguer's bucket and 'author' is the name of the collection, so the record does not say what a reader is opening.
structure_note: Not one work: a set of fragments, each photograph showing two pecha leaves (or the two sides of one) on a board with tapes, pins and the archivist's sticky note, so printed backsteps (2) and repeats (5) are expected. p56 is a board with only a sticky note. Counters disagree: 135 page records have OCR but the pages_ocr field says 59; 55 of 157 are translated.

book_verdict: A catalogue bucket of fragments rather than a book: photographs of leaf pairs and separator cards, a BDRC read of cursive script full of impossible stacks, and a fluent translation over it that gets ritual measures wrong. I read dbu med poorly at this size, so the page scores are low-confidence; the unit and structure problems are not.
